title: Super source follower
description: A super source follower (SSF): a plain source follower whose output resistance is driven down by a local feedback device. The input follower sets the DC level shift (the output sits about one input $V_{GS}$ below the input), and the feedback device senses the follower current and closes a local loop that lowers the output resistance by the loop gain $g_{m,fb}/g_{ds,in}$ (the feedback transconductance into the follower's own output resistance): $R_{out} \approx g_{ds,in}/((g_{m,in} + g_{mb,in}) * g_{m,fb})$, versus $1/g_{m,in}$ for a plain follower. That makes it a compact low-impedance buffer. The feedback is a local loop; its own phase margin (whether that loop is stable) is a small-signal AC check the simulator owns, out of this sheet's scope — this sheet sizes the DC operating point and the low-frequency output resistance only. On the demo NMOS table both devices size against the same data.

params.name: I_in
params.note: current through the input follower device (held fixed by the bias source, which linearizes the buffer)

params.name: gm_id_fb
params.note: feedback device inversion: at fixed I_fb it sets gm_fb, and with it the loop gain gm_fb/gds_in

params.name: L_fb
params.note: the loop gain gm_fb/gds_in does not depend on L_fb (gm_fb is set by gm_id_fb and I_fb), so this knob moves the feedback device's vdsat and area, not Rout

doc.title: Input follower device
doc.description: The source-follower input device carrying a fixed current; its gm sets the base output resistance and its vgs the DC level shift.

doc.title: Feedback device
doc.description: The local-feedback device that senses the follower current; its transconductance into the follower's output resistance, gm_fb/gds_in, is the loop gain that lowers the output resistance.

rows.name: gm_in
rows.note: input follower transconductance (sets the plain-follower output resistance 1/gm_in)

rows.name: av0_fb
rows.note: reference reading of the feedback device's own intrinsic gain; the loop gain that Rout actually divides by is gm_fb/gds_in, not this

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: SSF output resistance: the local loop drives the follower's own output conductance down by the product of the two transconductances. The gds is the INPUT device's — it is the input device whose drain current the loop senses — and the source-body generator adds to gm because the output node is the input device's source. On a sky130 tt realization of this buffer this form lands within 3% of the measured 56 ohm

rows.name: Rout_plain
rows.note: the plain source-follower output resistance, for comparison

rows.name: level_shift
rows.note: output sits about one input Vgs below the input (source-follower DC level shift)

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents, taken as the input device's whole gate capacitance. It OVERSTATES what a driver sees — the source follows the gate near unity, bootstrapping most of the gate-source capacitance away. No rule reads it

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — ONE stacked branch: the feedback device reuses the input device's current rather than drawing its own, so the supply pays for it once. A realization that biases the output node with a source of its own adds that current on top. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rules.note: the buffer output resistance meets the target
input follower device stays saturated at its operating vds
feedback device stays saturated at its operating vds
